subject: physics
title: Work, Energy and Power
meta: Lesson practice set · Question types of the April 2026 NIOS paper
instructions: Practice set for this lesson in the question types of the April 2026 paper.
Where a question has OR, answer either one.
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

questions.q: A long spring stretched by 2 cm has potential energy V. If it is stretched by 10 cm, its potential energy will be —
questions.work:
U = ½kx², so U ∝ x².
x increases 5 times (2 cm → 10 cm), so U = 5² × V = 25V.

questions.q: The area under a force–displacement graph equals —
If the speed of a body is doubled, its kinetic energy increases by —
questions.work: K ∝ v². Doubling v makes K four times, i.e. an increase of 4K − K = 3K = 300%.

questions.q: A crane lifts 100 kg through 10 m in 20 s (g = 10 m/s²). Its power is —
Two bodies of different masses have equal momentum. Then —
options: the lighter body has more kinetic energy
the heavier body has more kinetic energy
questions.work: K = p²/2m. With p the same, K is larger for the smaller m.

questions.q: In which case is work done against the gravity of the earth?
options: A monkey climbs up a tree
A car moves on a level road
A person tries to lift a heavy load but fails
A person lifts a load in an orbiting satellite

questions.q: A particle is projected at 60° to the horizontal with kinetic energy E. Its kinetic energy at the highest point is —
questions.work:
At the top only the horizontal velocity u cos 60° = u/2 remains.
KE = ½m(u/2)² = ¼ × ½mu² = E/4.

questions.q: A 2 kg body moves at a constant 5 m/s under a constant 3 N force. The power lost to friction is —
questions.work:
Constant velocity ⇒ friction = applied force = 3 N.
Power lost = Fv = 3 × 5 = 15 W.

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (fill in the blanks, true/false, match or one word).

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (a) The SI unit of energy is ______. (b) 1 horsepower = ______ watt.
(a) What angle between force and displacement gives maximum work? (b) A light and a heavy body have the same momentum — which has more KE?
State True or False: (a) Work done by a conservative force over a closed path is zero. (b) In an inelastic collision momentum is not conserved.
questions.answer:
(a) True.
(b) False — momentum is conserved in all collisions; only KE is lost.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (a) 1 kWh is a unit of ______. (b) Joule per second is also called ______.
Complete: (a) A spring of k = 100 N/m stretched by 10 cm stores ______ J. (b) If the stretch is doubled, the energy becomes ______ times.
(a) Two bodies stick together after collision — elastic or inelastic? (b) Name the energy stored in a stretched spring.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: What are conservative forces? Give one example.
questions.answer: A force is conservative if the work it does is independent of the path and zero over any closed path, so mechanical energy is conserved. Examples: gravitational force, spring force, electrostatic force.

questions.q: A 100 kg body is lifted 8 m in 10 s. Calculate the power supplied. (g = 9.8 m/s²)
Convert (a) 7460 W into hp and (b) 360 kJ into kWh.
A particle moving with kinetic energy 3.6 J hits a spring of force constant 180 N/m. Find the maximum compression.
questions.answer:
All the KE becomes spring energy: ½kx² = 3.6.
x² = 2 × 3.6/180 = 0.04 ⇒ x = 0.2 m.

questions.q: A ball is thrown vertically up. Where is its (i) kinetic energy and (ii) potential energy maximum?
questions.answer:
(i) KE is maximum at the point of projection (and on return), where speed is greatest.
(ii) PE is maximum at the highest point, where it momentarily stops.

questions.q: Two particles of different masses have equal kinetic energies. Find the ratio of their momenta and velocities.
questions.answer:
K = p²/2m ⇒ p = √(2mK), so p₁/p₂ = √(m₁/m₂).
K = ½mv² ⇒ v = √(2K/m), so v₁/v₂ = √(m₂/m₁).

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: What is meant by positive, negative and zero work? Give an example of each.
questions.answer:
W = Fd cos θ.
Positive work (θ < 90°): a person lifting a bucket — force and displacement are both upward.
Negative work (θ > 90°): friction on a sliding body acts opposite to its displacement.
Zero work (θ = 90° or d = 0): a coolie carrying a load on level ground — the upward force is perpendicular to the horizontal motion.

or.q: State whether the work is positive, negative or zero: (a) friction on a body sliding down an incline; (b) a man lifting a bucket out of a well; (c) a coolie walking on a level platform with a load.
or.answer:
(a) Negative — friction acts up the incline, opposite to the motion.
(b) Positive — the force and the displacement are both upward.
(c) Zero — the force (upward support) is perpendicular to the horizontal displacement.

questions.q: A force F = (5i + 3j) N moves a particle through d = (3i + 4j) m. Calculate the work done.
A 2 kg body falls freely from 10 m. Using the work–energy principle find (a) its speed at 6 m above the ground, (b) its speed on reaching the ground and (c) the work done by gravity. (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.answer:
(a) It has fallen 4 m: ½mv² = mg × 4 ⇒ v = √(2 × 10 × 4) = √80 ≈ 8.9 m/s.
(b) Fallen 10 m: v = √(2 × 10 × 10) = √200 ≈ 14.1 m/s.
(c) W = mgh = 2 × 10 × 10 = 200 J, equal to the gain in KE.

questions.q: Water falls 51 m at 108 kg per second in a hydroelectric plant. Calculate the work done per second and the power. (g = 9.8 m/s²)
questions.answer:
Work per second = mgh = 108 × 9.8 × 51 ≈ 5.4 × 10⁴ J.
Power (ideal) = 5.4 × 10⁴ J/s ≈ 54 kW.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: State and prove the work–energy theorem. A 10 kg body moving at 4 m/s is acted on by 30 N for 2 s. Find (a) its final speed, (b) the distance covered, (c) the work done and (d) its initial and final KE.
questions.answer:
Theorem: the work done by the net force on a body equals the change in its kinetic energy.
Proof (constant force): v² = u² + 2as ⇒ ½mv² − ½mu² = mas = Fs = W.
(a) a = 30/10 = 3 m/s²; v = 4 + 3 × 2 = 10 m/s.
(b) s = ut + ½at² = 8 + 6 = 14 m.
(c) W = Fs = 30 × 14 = 420 J.
(d) Kᵢ = ½ × 10 × 16 = 80 J; K_f = ½ × 10 × 100 = 500 J. Check: 500 − 80 = 420 J = W.

or.q: Give an example of a variable force and derive the work done by it.
or.answer:
A spring force F = −kx varies with the extension x.
The work done in stretching by a small dx is dW = kx dx. Total work from 0 to x: W = ∫₀ˣ kx dx = ½kx².
This is the area of the triangle under the F–x graph and is stored as elastic potential energy in the spring.

questions.q: A 10 g bullet moving at 100 m/s embeds in a 1 kg wooden block at rest. Find (a) the velocity after collision, (b) the KE before and after, (c) whether the collision is elastic, and (d) the energy lost.
questions.answer:
(a) Momentum is conserved: 0.01 × 100 = (0.01 + 1)v ⇒ v = 1/1.01 ≈ 0.99 m/s.
(b) Before: ½ × 0.01 × 100² = 50 J. After: ½ × 1.01 × 0.99² ≈ 0.495 J.
(c) Perfectly inelastic — the bodies stick together and KE is not conserved.
(d) Loss ≈ 50 − 0.5 = 49.5 J, which becomes heat, sound and work in deforming the wood.

questions.q: Ball A (1 kg) moving at 20 m/s along +x collides elastically with ball B (2 kg) moving at 10 m/s along −x. Find their velocities after the collision.
questions.answer:
Momentum and kinetic energy are both conserved.
v_A = [(m_A − m_B)u_A + 2m_Bu_B]/(m_A + m_B) = [(1 − 2) × 20 + 2 × 2 × (−10)]/3 = (−20 − 40)/3 = −20 m/s.
v_B = [(m_B − m_A)u_B + 2m_Au_A]/(m_A + m_B) = [(2 − 1)(−10) + 2 × 1 × 20]/3 = 30/3 = 10 m/s.
So A rebounds at 20 m/s along −x and B moves at 10 m/s along +x.
Check: momentum before = 20 − 20 = 0; after = −20 + 20 = 0.
